text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple DNS SERVFAILs observed from AZ-C (eu-west-1c) for internal zone redwood.internal. High connection retries and 502s reported by health checks. Automatic paging to SRE-oncall.

mike (sre-oncall): I'm on it. seeing spike in 5xxs from endpoints in az-c. grabbing query logs.

jess (netops): I see a flurry of route table re-associations in az-c around 09:12 UTC. Could be terraform rollout or automation.

mike (sre-oncall): can someone run tcpdump on the dns resolver in az-c? suspect UDP drops or asymmetric return path.

samir (eng-runtime): running: `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53 -c 200` now, will paste samples.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: detect-change: route_table_association rta-0c123 -> subnet-azc-priv at 2026-03-15T09:11:33Z by terraform-runner

jess (netops): that's the noisy change. policy auto-rollout for env=prod started. I'm pausing the rollout for az-c.

mike (sre-oncall): sample tcpdump: `;; -> query: service.redis.redwood.internal A` followed by no response for ~250ms then `SERVFAIL`. conntrack shows many NAT timeouts. I think NAT path is dropping return traffic.

tara (prod-support): customer ops: several customers reporting internal errors for embedding endpoints, high latency and retries. Partial impact in eu and na-west. forwarding list.

elena (customer-ops): confirmed: 7 paying customers with 5xx spikes tied to az-c. alerted account teams. urgent status page update?

mike (sre-oncall): set incident severity P1. live mitigation: move traffic away from az-c by adjusting smart-routing to prefer az-b for affected model routes. Samir, can you toggle routing weight?

samir (eng-runtime): applying temporary routing policy: `route_weight[model-v2,az-c]=0.0` `route_weight[model-v2,az-b]=1.0` -- applying now.

ops-bot: routing-config: rollout successful to control-plane at 09:20 UTC. Active requests draining from az-c.

jess (netops): while reroute buys time, we need to fix pipeline: observed conntrack table near max on many nat instances in az-c: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` shows 196k of 196k.

mike (sre-oncall): increase conntrack max on nat instances in az-c: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and persist via cloud-init. pushing commands now via ad-hoc runner.

samir (eng-runtime): also enabling TCP keepalive tuning on the runtime workers to reduce ephemeral port churn.

jess (netops): found misapplied route table: a route table intended for staging was associated with a subset of prod private subnets in az-c, causing return path to jump to a different NAT cluster and drop ICMP/UDP. rolling back association to rtb-prod-azc.

ops-bot: route_table_association rta-0c123 rollback initiated by jess at 09:33 UTC.

mike (sre-oncall): after rollback + conntrack bump + routing weight cutover, errors drop. health checks show recovery to 99.8% for model-v2 within 6 minutes.

elena (customer-ops): customers with support tickets notified of mitigation and ETA for full remediation. asking for RCA blurb.

jess (netops): root cause: automation had a tag-matching bug where `env=prod` and `env=staging` both matched due to a malformed regex, triggered association for ~4 subnets. patching automation and adding unit test.

mike (sre-oncall): final steps: 1) open incident ticket, 2) run full conntrack scrub and remove stale NAT entries, 3) revert temporary routing after we confirm stability, 4) schedule postmortem w/ owners. handing off to jess for the deep fix.

jess (netops): ack. I'll own the rollback PR and test in canary then a safe re-roll. ETA for full fix and redeploy at ~2 hours.

pagerduty: mike acknowledged the incident at 09:14 UTC.

mike (sre-oncall): handing off to jess for follow-up and postmortem. I'm available if escalation needed.

jess (netops): Handoff accepted. updating incident channel and will post timeline, metrics, and RCA when ready. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident-status: mitigated -> monitoring at 09:40 UTC.

mike (sre-oncall): closing active paging. last note: need test for route table tag-safety and add alerts for conntrack >80% rather than only 95%.

elena (customer-ops): posting customer-facing blurb: "We experienced increased errors for some API calls due to a networking misconfiguration in one availability zone. Traffic was rerouted and the issue mitigated; we will follow up with an RCA."

jess (netops): thanks all. I'll put a short summary in /incidents and schedule the postmortem invite.

End of thread.
